name: phi-4-mini-adr-detector
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct (config.json max_position_embeddings 131072). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
notes: ADDED 2026-10-31. A LoRA (r=32, qkv/o/gate_up/down) SFT of microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct, fully merged here - identical tensor set and config, 3.836B. Recorded because the card prints base and this model in ONE ADR-Bench table: balanced accuracy 72.7 vs 55.0 and F1 0.481 vs 0.263 on the triage-prompt base row. Honest caveat: RAW accuracy is a LOSS (82.2 vs 86.5 on the neutral-prompt base row) and the card itself flags 59.5% malicious recall and 0.403 precision. Uber ADR-Bench 303 traces, held out from training. Licence MIT, repo created 2026-09-01.

benchmarks.name: ADR-Bench balanced accuracy
benchmarks.config: Card table '| Model | Benign | Malicious | Accuracy | Balanced acc | F1 |': 'This model' 72.7 vs 'Phi-4-mini base (ADR triage prompt)' 55.0. Uber ADR-Bench, 303 traces (261 benign / 42 malicious), held out from training, zero truncation at 131K context.

benchmarks.name: ADR-Bench F1
benchmarks.config: Same table, F1 0.481 vs the same base row 0.263. The base has a second row ('neutral prompt') at 0.163 and 54.2 balanced acc; the triage-prompt row is the apples-to-apples setting.

benchmarks.name: ADR-Bench raw accuracy
benchmarks.config: Same table: 82.2 vs base(neutral) 86.5 - a LOSS on raw accuracy. Base(triage) 27.7. Card argues raw accuracy is a trap: labelling every trace benign scores 86.1 on this class imbalance.
